title: Evaluation of the Storage Stability of Extracellular Vesicles
protocol: Cultivate cells under conditions required for the respective cell line.
Culture cells for 24-72 hours in serum-free conditions or medium containing EV-depleted fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Centrifuge the medium at 300 x g for 10 minutes to pellet cells.
Collect the cell-conditioned medium without disturbing the pelleted cells.
Store the collected cell-conditioned medium overnight at 4 °C if necessary.
Use freshly produced cell-conditioned medium directly if possible.
Culture HUVEC cells for 120 hours in EGM-2 medium containing FBS and other supplements.
Culture HUVEC cells for 48 hours in EBM-2 basal medium free of additional supplements.
Centrifuge the conditioned medium at 3,000 x g for 15 minutes at 4 °C to remove cell debris.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to the UC tubes.
Mark the orientation of the tubes in the centrifuge for retrieval of EV pellet after UC if using a fixed angle rotor.
Centrifuge for 2 hours at 120,000 x g with a k-factor of 259.4.
Carefully discard the supernatant using a serological pipet to avoid disturbing the pelleted EVs.
Add 200 µL of 0.2 µm-filtered phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the first tube.
Resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down with PBS and residual supernatant.
Transfer the resulting EV suspension to the next tube for resuspension.
Proceed similarly to resuspend all EVs in a final volume of approximately 300-350 µL.
Confirm the presence of particles using nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA).
Use optimized settings for the given EV type, such as screen gain of 1.0 and camera level of 13 for recording three videos of 30 s each.
Analyze with a screen gain of 1.0 and detection threshold of 5.
Use the pellet immediately if possible; otherwise store it at 4 °C overnight.
To the resuspended pellet, add beta-glucuronidase (10 mg/mL in PBS) to a final concentration of 1.5 mg/mL and saponin (10 mg/mL in H2O) to a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Mix well by vortexing for 3 s.
Incubate the mixture for 10 min at room temperature with intermitted mixing by gently flicking the tube.
Purify the incubated sample directly by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC).
Dissolve DMPC and DPPC in a 2:3 molar ratio in chloroform to a final concentration of 5 mM for liposome preparation.
Prepare 1 mL aliquots in HPLC vials and let them dry overnight to form a lipid film.
Rehydrate the lipid-film with 1 mL of PBS containing 1.5 mg/mL glucuronidase.
Heat it to 42 °C and vortex for 1 min.
Heat the extruder assembly to 42 °C and extrude the lipid suspension 11x through a 200 nm polycarbonate membrane.
Purify the liposome sample directly by SEC.
Use only fresh purified water and freshly prepared buffers.
Filter all buffers through a 0.2 μm membrane filter.
Degas buffers to prevent air bubble formation in the column.
Centrifuge SEC medium at 3,000 x g for 10 min to remove EtOH.
Replace EtOH with degassed water after centrifugation.
Fill a glass column (inner diameter 10 mm) with SEC medium to the 15 mL mark.
Let the gel settle completely before use.
Equilibrate the column with at least two column volumes of PBS before a run.
Wash the column with one column volume of water before storage.
Store the column by adding at least two column volumes of 20% EtOH.
Re-wash the column with one column volume of water after storage.
Equilibrate the column again with PBS before re-use.
Use up to 400 μL of EV or liposome suspension in each separation.
Collect fractions of 1 mL during SEC.
Confirm the separation of EVs and liposomes from contaminating proteins and free glucuronidase.
Correlate particle concentrations of collected fractions with protein concentration and glucuronidase activity.
Assess particle concentration by NTA.
Assess protein content by bicinchoninic acid (BCA) assay or another suitable protein quantification assay.
Perform the assay according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Assess glucuronidase activity by glucuronidase assay.
Optionally, assess EV morphology by transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
Add 10 µL of EV suspension to a TEM grid.
Incubate for 10 min.
Blot away any excess liquid using filter paper.
Fix with 10 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min.
Blot away any excess.
Wash 3x with water.
Stain vesicles by incubating with 30 µL of 1% phospho-tungstic acid hydrate for 20 s.
After blotting, dry the vesicles overnight.
Visualize by TEM.
Optionally, assess EV morphology by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Fix previously prepared TEM samples onto carbon disks.
Sputter them with a 50 nm thick gold layer.
Visualize by SEM.
Measure the particle concentration of the sample by NTA.
Add 1 µL of fluorescein di-β-D-glucuronide (10 mg/mL in H2O) to 199 µL of PBS to prepare a working solution.
Mix 25 µL of the working solution with 125 µL of purified EVs to achieve a final concentration of 8.3 µg/mL.
Pipette the mixture into a black 96-well plate.
Measure time point 0 h using a plate reader at an excitation wavelength of 480 nm and emission wavelength of 516 nm.
Cover the plate tightly with transparent plastic foil to minimize evaporation.
Incubate the plate in the dark for 18 h at 37 °C.
Measure fluorescein production using the parameters listed in step 6.2.
Store EV samples at 4 °C or -80 °C as required.
Add trehalose (40 mg/mL in H2O) to purified EVs up to a final concentration of 4 mg/mL for lyophilization.
Freeze the treated samples at -80 °C for at least 1 h.
Lyophilize the samples with a shelf temperature of 15 °C and pressure of 0.180 mbar for 46 hours.
Set the shelf temperature to 25 °C and pressure to 0.0035 mbar for final drying for 2 hours.
Store the lyophilized samples at 4 °C.
Rehydrate the samples by adding an equal volume of water as the initial EV suspension (typically, 400 μL).
Remove free glucuronidase from the rehydrated samples through purification using SEC or AF4.
Set up the instrument for AF4 with a small channel and a 350 µm spacer.
Use a 30 kD molecular weight cut-off cellulose membrane in the AF4 setup.
Place a 0.1 μm pore size filter between the HPLC pump and the AF4 channel.
Use freshly prepared 0.1 μm-filtered PBS as the mobile phase to reduce particle load and noise.
Detect proteins using a UV detector set to 280 nm.
Use multiangle light scattering with the laser set to 658 nm to detect particles.
Pre-focus for 1 min with a focus flow of 1 mL/min.
Inject 300 µL of the sample at a rate of 0.2 mL/min.
Keep up the focus flow for 10 min after injection.
Elute the sample at 1 mL/min while applying a cross flow that decreases from 2 mL/min to 0.1 mL/min over the course of 8 min.
Elute for another 10 min without cross flow.
Collect fractions of 1 mL, starting after 12.5 min and continuing until 27 min.
Perform the glucuronidase assay as described above (see section 6).
Use the NTA as described above (see step 2.5) to assess the size and concentration.
Optionally perform TEM and SEM to assess the morphology of the EVs after storage (see 5.3).
